To the FAO Internship Programme Team,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the FAO Internship Programme at Headquarters in Rome, and specifically in the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (IYRP) Chinese Working Group - Institutional Liaison Assistant internship. I am a full-time undergraduate student in English Language and Literature (minor in Finance) at Jilin University, China, expected to graduate in June 2028, and a national of an FAO Member State.
Why I want to join FAO
FAO's mandate - to defeat hunger, advance sustainable agri-food systems, and translate evidence into the Four Betters (Better Production, Better Nutrition, Better Environment, Better Life) - maps directly onto my academic and practical path. I want to learn how multilateral policy on food security and sustainable production is researched, negotiated, and delivered to member countries. I am especially drawn to FAO's work on rangelands and pastoralist livelihoods, which sits at the crossroads of livestock, sustainable land management, and resilient food systems.
Why my background fits this role
My most relevant experience is my assistantship with the UN International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (IYRP) Working Group. Supporting this UN observance gave me first-hand exposure to how rangeland sustainability and pastoralist livelihoods connect to FAO's mandate. I helped maintain a 100+ record expert database and coordinated multilingual materials, work that mirrors the data organisation, monitoring, and stakeholder liaison this liaison role requires.
This is reinforced by agriculture-related studies and field exposure that grounded my understanding of food production and rural livelihoods, and by development-cooperation experience: twelve bilingual translation sessions for MOFCOM foreign-aid programmes serving 80+ participants from 15+ countries, plus involvement in BRICS and SDG initiatives. These taught me how international development cooperation operates on the ground.
A distinctive asset is language: as a native Mandarin speaker with IELTS 7.5, I command two of FAO's official languages (Chinese and English). For the IYRP Chinese Working Group, this bilingual capacity directly supports Chinese-language promotion, institutional liaison with Chinese partners, and the UNFCCC observer accreditation process, where accurate cross-language communication matters.
How I will contribute
In this Institutional Liaison Assistant role I can support the IYRP Chinese Working Group by helping prepare and track the UNFCCC observer accreditation application, drafting and translating Chinese-language promotion materials, maintaining partner and expert databases, and coordinating outreach across institutions. My skills in Python and MySQL for data cleaning, qualitative coding for structured analysis, and Microsoft Office for reporting would let me contribute to research, dashboards, and technical writing from day one. At the China-Northeast Asia Expo I coordinated foreign-guest reception for 200+ delegates across six departments, evidence that I can manage logistics and stakeholder liaison reliably in a fast-paced, multicultural team.
I am available for a full-time internship of three months and open to a longer placement, meet the working-knowledge English requirement, and am committed to FAO's zero-fee, merit-based values. Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to support FAO's mission.
